gist: Milo Riley-Smith's documentary covers a mass shooting at Sydney's Bondi beach.
Jewish Australians felt less safe following events of 7 October 2023.
The film uses multiple perspectives and footage to document the six-minute attack.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Fifteen people died when two men shot at defenceless families from a footbridge at Bondi beach during Hanukah festivities. A clock tracked the six-minute ordeal. Lifeguards used shark-bite training for gunshot wounds, a woman filmed from a building, Nick documented the event with a camera, and Ahmed Al Ahmed tackled an attacker and snatched his weapon.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Participants felt less safe after the 7 October 2023 attack on Israel and subsequent bombardment of Gaza, noting a flaring of antisemitic violence and rhetoric. The documentary stands as a memorial to victims and a warning about where hatred can lead, while questioning whether Australian authorities did enough to protect them.

gist: Dwain Hall was found guilty of kidnapping and murdering British woman Sonia Exelby.
Hall lured Exelby to Florida after grooming her on a fetish website.
Exelby struggled with mental illness, and Hall received a life sentence in prison.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A Florida jury convicted 54-year-old mechanic Dwain Hall of kidnapping and first-degree murder, sentencing him to life in prison. Hall groomed 32-year-old Sonia Exelby online before she travelled from England to Florida in October 2025. Exelby, from Southsea, Hampshire (reported as Portsmouth in The Guardian), had mental illness and sought someone to end her life. Hall drove her from an airport to a rental, stabbed her to death, and buried her. Hall's defence claimed she took her own life.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Prosecutors stated Hall exploited Exelby's vulnerabilities for sadistic gratification. Exelby's family criticised predatory fetish websites, welcomed the verdict, and pledged to fight for mental health awareness in her memory.

fivew: Dwain Hall, a 54-year-old mechanic, and Sonia Exelby, a 32-year-old British music teacher.
Dwain Hall was convicted of kidnapping and first-degree murder and sentenced to life imprisonment.
Hall was convicted on Friday following Exelby's disappearance and death in October 2025.
A court in Ocala, Marion County, Florida.
Prosecutors said Hall exploited Exelby's severe mental illness and suicidal thoughts for sadistic pleasure.

gist: The UK is expected to experience its coldest night of autumn so far.
Temperatures could fall to minus 10C in rural Scotland overnight on Friday.
Cold weather health alerts are active alongside 12 flood alerts across England.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Thursday night brought temperatures down to minus 8.4C at Tulloch Bridge in the Scottish Highlands, making it the coldest night of autumn until Friday. Cold Arctic air has moved southwards across the UK, bringing frost, rain, and wintry showers to northern areas while southern regions remained milder.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The UK Health Security Agency issued yellow cold health alerts for parts of northern England until Monday morning due to potential impacts on healthcare services and vulnerable people. Additionally, 12 flood alerts are active in England. The colder autumn weather also boosted supermarket clothing sales volume by 1.5 per cent, helping overall retail sales recover unexpectedly.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Friday night is forecast to become the coldest of autumn so far, with temperatures potentially reaching minus 10C in rural Scotland. Widespread frost will develop across the Midlands, northern England, Northern Ireland and Scotland. Saturday is expected to be mostly dry with sunshine.

sections.text: British retail sales surged by 0.7% in October as the public responded to the government's Be Ready emergency preparedness campaign by buying long-life food, tinned goods, and UHT milk. Clothing, footwear, and gallery visits also increased, though motor fuel sales fell by 2.2%.

Mamdani announces plan to close New York's Rikers Island jail by 2032

gist: Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced a plan to close New York's Rikers Island jail by 2032.
The proposal involves building four new jails and reducing the detainee population to 4,100.
The correction officers' union criticized the plan, while officials defended the approach.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Mayor Zohran Mamdani unveiled a plan on Friday to close the Rikers Island jail complex by 2032. The proposal includes building four new jails in Brooklyn, the Bronx, Queens and Manhattan, and reducing the detainee population from over 6,500 to 4,100. Previous closure plans faced delays under former Mayor Eric Adams' administration and due to the Covid pandemic. The City Council must approve the updated timeline.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Rikers Island has faced severe backlash over staffing shortages, crumbling conditions and nine inmate deaths this year. Supporters describe the closure as a generational opportunity to transform detention and improve inmate outcomes. However, the New York City correction officers' union criticized the plan, arguing that an arbitrary cap on jail beds jeopardises public safety by potentially releasing violent felons.

gist: A truck killed three people at a Tsawwassen First Nation ceremony near Vancouver.
Police initially suggested a medical emergency, causing outrage as no driver was arrested.
Community members are gathering their own evidence due to a lack of answers.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A black pickup truck towing an equipment trailer breached a curb outside a mall near Vancouver, striking a group gathered for a Tsawwassen First Nation ceremony. Virginia Splockton and wilapiya were killed at the scene, and Gwenyth Brigid Dwyn died later in hospital. Minutes earlier, the same truck had struck another vehicle nearby. Police released the driver from the hospital the same day without charges, suggesting a preliminary medical emergency.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Families and community members are outraged by the lack of arrests and communication from Delta police. They argue officers rushed to conclusions about a medical emergency, leaving grieving families to gather their own evidence and video footage.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Police stated they are still investigating the movements of the vehicle and the possibility of a medical event, adding that charges would be laid if evidence establishes criminality.

fivew: Members of the Tsawwassen First Nation and the driver of the truck.

gist: A new study reveals most US prisoners were victims of violent crime before incarceration.
Experts argue that bolstering trauma recovery resources can help break the cycle of crime.
Jemaine Hunter shares his experience of childhood trauma and decades in prison.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A new study by Just Safe found that 84% of people in US prisons or jails were victims of violent crime before their first incarceration. The nationally representative survey of 20,000 Americans showed that half experienced caregiver abuse and one-third faced sexual or intimate partner violence.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Experts say the findings show the need to reframe crime politics by focusing on trauma recovery rather than punishment alone. Unaddressed pain can lead individuals to turn to drugs, alcohol, or further violence, trapping them in the justice system.

gist: Lenders for SpaceX's chip financing deal do not want collateral deployed into space.

SpaceX plans to use the chips in data centres within the US.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Lenders behind SpaceX's $40 billion chip financing deal reportedly asked that purchased chips not be used in orbit. It is unclear if SpaceX agreed, but credit rating reports state the chips will be used in US data centres.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Data centre financing relies on using chips as collateral for loans. Lenders cannot repossess chips orbiting Earth if a borrower defaults. Consequently, financing space data centres carries higher risks and expenses than terrestrial facilities.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: SpaceX is deploying compute at ground stations while working with Tesla to build a chip foundry named Terafab in the US. Elon Musk expects space data centres to become cost-effective in two to three years.

gist: Young people staged coordinated protests across European cities on Friday over rising living costs.
Demonstrators demanded increased spending on education and welfare alongside an end to militarisation.
Rallies occurred in countries including Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Portugal and the UK.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: On Friday, students and young workers held coordinated rallies in over 20 European countries. Organised by the Youth Strike coalition and other groups, demonstrators protested against rising living costs, housing shortages, underfunded education, and military spending. Rallies took place in Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Belgium, Greece, and the UK. In Italy, tens of thousands joined protests alongside a general strike called by the CGIL trade union against prime minister Giorgia Meloni's economic policies.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Activists claimed governments are ignoring youth priorities while cutting healthcare and education funding. Organisers called the rallies a step towards an international movement demanding social justice, welfare investment, an end to militarisation, and climate action.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Daniel Thomas live-streamed himself slashing an inflatable dinghy eight times in the English Channel on 22 September. Rescue crews were recovering the vessel after assisting migrants aboard. Thomas admitted criminal damage and was jailed for 15 months at Portsmouth Crown Court.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The judge described Thomas as a publicity seeker who deliberately disrupted essential border and rescue work. Outlets differed on his comments: The Guardian reported he said "everyone in these boats", whilst the BBC stated the court heard he said "every one of these boats".

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: His remand time will count towards his sentence. He faces a trial at Westminster Magistrates' Court in June regarding separate alleged offences in Dover.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Levent Alpöge claimed to have used Anthropic's Claude chatbot to prove the 170-year-old Riemann hypothesis over six weeks. The proof is over 250,000 pages long and written in the computer language Lean.

sections.text: The Riemann hypothesis is one of the most famous and difficult problems in mathematics. If verified, this achievement would mark a seismic milestone for artificial intelligence in higher mathematics, though verification could take considerable time.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The UK government negotiated a trade agreement with the EU to cut red tape, paperwork and border checks on food exports and imports. Supermarkets welcomed the announcement, but grocers have not committed to reducing food prices as a direct result.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Removing red tape could help smaller UK food exporters return to the EU single market. The government forecasts an economic gain of £5bn by 2040 from the food deal, and £17bn a year overall when combined with emission and youth mobility agreements. However, critics highlight that the deal requires aligning with EU regulations, such as pesticide rules, reducing regulatory freedom.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Full legal texts will reveal further details. The government will decide whether to use this food deal as a blueprint to seek single market alignment for other sectors, including cars and chemicals.

timeline.text: Prisons get OK to jam contraband phones. CTIA says nearby phones will be jammed too.

gist: The FCC voted to let state and local prisons use jamming technology.
CTIA warned that testing showed jammers would also block lawful calls nearby.
Wireless carriers and a commissioner raised legal and unintended consequence concerns.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Federal Communications Commission voted to allow state and local prisons and jails to use targeted jamming technology against contraband cellphones. While the FCC included safeguards requiring testing and community notice, wireless lobby group CTIA warned that testing showed jammers interfere with communications up to two and a half miles away and block 911 calls.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Prison officials and police groups supported the move, stating inmates use contraband phones to plan crimes, violent attacks, and drug trafficking. Conversely, critics and wireless carriers warned that jammers cannot differentiate between contraband and lawful devices, create safety hazards, and exceed the FCC's statutory authority.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Facilities wanting to use the technology must apply to the FCC, explain their deployment plans, and prove through testing that the signal remains inside the designated area. The FCC is also seeking comment on next steps, and the order could potentially face a legal challenge.

fivew: The FCC voted to permit state and local prisons to use targeted cellphone jamming technology.
To stop inmates from using contraband cellphones to plan crimes and attacks.

quotes.text: Today, we are finally authorizing state and local prisons and jails to use targeted jamming against contraband cell phones for the first time.
The technology has advanced to the point where it can be focused with geographic precision.

timeline.text: Murray Warren obituary

gist: Murray Warren was an influential teacher known for avoiding punishment.
He overcame significant physical challenges from childhood health issues and amputation.
His career spanned ministry, headship, coaching, and mentoring in diverse settings.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Murray Warren died at the age of 88. Born in London with a club foot, he spent his early years receiving corrective hospital treatment. After studying at London Bible College, he chose to have his leg amputated below the knee at age 22. He was ordained as a Baptist minister in 1963 before retraining as a teacher. He later served as head at Howbridge junior school and Broomfield primary school, eventually tutoring excluded adolescent boys for the Essex education department.

sections.text: Three French police officers were convicted of a racist assault on music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in November 2020. gist: Generative AI tools promise to help shoppers find Black Friday deals.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Shoppers are increasingly considering generative AI tools to help navigate Black Friday bargains. When tested with a search for a 55-inch TV deal, popular free AI models provided mixed results, including out-of-stock items, incorrect sizing information, full-price listings instead of deals, and sponsored links.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Inaccurate pricing and outdated data in AI results can waste shoppers' time or cause them to miss out on actual savings. Experts warn that users should not take chatbot advice at face value, as advertising models may start to influence recommendations.

sections.heading: What happens next

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: French artist Philippe Parreno opened his first major Australian exhibition, 5 Moons, at the Museum of Contemporary Art in Sydney. The multi-level exhibition features kinetic objects, screens, sound, and lighting connected across the museum. These installations are driven by real-time weather and environmental data captured from an abandoned almond farm in Spain.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The exhibition explores deep philosophical questions about human perception and our relationship with the landscape. By using data from a remote desert to dictate conditions in a Sydney gallery, Parreno challenges visitors to consider how nature and environments interact.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The exhibition is scheduled to remain on display at the Museum of Contemporary Art in Sydney until 26 April 2027.

gist: Filmmaker Parvinder Shergill explores dual cultural identities in her new film Touché.
The film features a British South Asian protagonist who discovers fencing to change her life.
Shergill aims to inspire audiences while addressing mental health and personal trauma.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: British Indian filmmaker Parvinder Shergill has produced a new film titled Touché. The story follows a character named Deep, who takes up fencing to transform her life. The film features a cast including Matthew Lewis, Paul Chowdhry, and Stephen Fry. It recently won the Tongues on Fire Flame Award at the UK Asian Film Festival.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Shergill highlights the importance of representing female South Asian protagonists in Western media. By blending visual storytelling with themes of mental health and personal trauma, she seeks to normalise difficult conversations within the South Asian community. The project also addresses the lack of diverse stunt performers in the industry.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Touché is scheduled for a theatrical release in cinemas starting from 27 November. Shergill is also working on a future science fiction project.

fivew: Filmmaker and actor Parvinder Shergill created and stars in the film.
The film Touché follows a woman who takes up fencing to change her life.
The film will be released in cinemas on 27 November.
The film is set in Britain.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Prof Peter Hindmarsh, an expert witness in the Lucy Letby trial, was excluded from clinical practice by his employer, University College London hospitals trust, in March 2023. The trust cited safety concerns regarding his advice on insulin. Despite this, Hindmarsh later provided a crucial expert report for a prosecution against Damion and Tamara Thomas. The jury in the Letby trial was not informed of his exclusion, and the Crown Prosecution Service only learned of the General Medical Council investigation into Hindmarsh in November 2025.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The case raises significant questions regarding the use of expert witnesses in court. Legal rules require experts to disclose information that could undermine their credibility or impartiality. Hindmarsh’s failure to disclose his regulatory issues until long after writing his report has led to concerns about whether he complied with these disclosure obligations and whether his evidence was appropriately scrutinised.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Anthropic went public on the Nasdaq, pricing its IPO at $83 a share before it rose to $111. The lab behind Claude became one of the most valuable companies on the planet amid peak AI hype. Competitors like OpenAI reportedly let Anthropic go public first to test market reactions and observe how investors value competitor revenue.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Anthropic must balance its commitment to AI safety branding with the profit-oriented demands of the public markets and increasing compute bills totalling roughly $900 billion. Its business model relies heavily on convincing enterprise and government customers to pay for safe, trustworthy AI despite increasing price sensitivity and cheaper open-source alternatives.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The upcoming quarters will reveal whether Anthropic can drive the massive revenue growth needed to deliver a return to investors. Analysts estimate significant revenue increases will be required to fund new models while maintaining expensive safety efforts under complex governance.

sections.text: Joshua Foster approached a fourth-floor hotel window in Cyprus with his two-year-old son, Jaxon. Foster was fined €3,000 after pleading guilty to causing death through a reckless, rash or dangerous act.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: UN talks in Geneva on establishing a legally binding treaty to control autonomous weapons collapsed. All-night negotiations failed to reach consensus after Russia filibustered and other military powers, including the US, resisted binding rules. Consequently, the UN forum adopted a weaker, non-binding mandate to continue talks.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: More than 100 countries sought new international rules, warning that AI-enabled weapons pose grave risks to civilians. Critics highlighted that states have discussed regulations for 13 years while autonomous targeting systems are already being used in active conflicts.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Countries will continue non-binding discussions, though past failures may lead states to seek alternative routes outside the UN forum to establish binding treaties.

timeline.text: The FBI and USDA were reportedly hacked

gist: The FBI and USDA have reportedly been targeted in separate cyber attacks.
The FBI breach targeted the National Crime Information Center used by law enforcement.
The USDA hack affected a payments database, raising concerns over sensitive data.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Reports indicate that both the FBI and the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) were hacked. CNN reported that the FBI intrusion targeted the National Crime Information Center, marking the agency's second attack in recent months. Meanwhile, NBC and Reuters reported that the USDA breach affected a payments database, which former officials warned might allow access to sensitive research and food safety data. President Donald Trump later confirmed the FBI breach in an interview with Fox News.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The breaches follow recent hacks at the FBI and DHS, as well as outages across the FAA and NSA. Former officials warned the USDA intrusion could provide access to sensitive data, including research on animal-borne illnesses. Following the recent outages, White House national cyber director Sean Cairncross stepped down.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Transport for London detected suspicious activity on its photocard website, leading to a cyber breach that compromised personal data of approximately 265,000 customers. Names, addresses, contact details, dates of birth and security questions were accessed. Transport for London took the website offline to limit access and reported the incident to the Information Commissioner's Office. Financial details and journey history were not compromised.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: This incident exposes personal details for a large number of customers and marks the second time in just over two years that the system has faced a cyber disruption, following a previous attack in September 2024.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The photocard website remains offline while investigations continue. Customers are currently unable to apply for or renew photocards online, though they can continue to travel and may contact customer services for assistance.

fivew: Personal details of Oyster photocard customers were accessed in a cyber breach.
Suspicious activity was detected on the photocard website.

gist: Manchester United's managerial hiring and firing costs approach £100m since 2013.
The club borrowed £10m shortly after confirming Mauricio Pochettino as head coach.
Michael Carrick was sacked with the club in the relegation zone.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Manchester United appointed Mauricio Pochettino on a two-and-a-half-year deal and will pay £7.5m in compensation to US Soccer. The club borrowed £10m three days later. Michael Carrick was sacked as manager last week after the club entered the relegation zone.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The latest compensation package pushes the total spent on hiring and firing managers since Sir Alex Ferguson retired to £95m, with costs expected to exceed £100m. United's overall revolving credit debt reached £240m, alongside outstanding transfer fees of £417m.

gist: Leon Smith is stepping down as Great Britain Davis Cup captain after seventeen years.
He guided the team to a historic title victory in 2015.
His final tournament in charge will be the upcoming Finals in Bologna.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Great Britain Davis Cup captain Leon Smith announced he is leaving his post after nearly seventeen years. He will step down following the upcoming Finals in Bologna. The Lawn Tennis Association has spoken to potential candidates but has not yet named a successor.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Smith took charge in 2010 when the team faced relegation. He successfully revived the squad and led them to their first title since 1936 in the year 2015, supported by player Andy Murray.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Smith hopes to achieve another successful run at the Bologna Finals. Afterwards, he will remain in his position as the head of British men's tennis while the LTA searches for his replacement.

quotes.text: It has been an enormous privilege to lead the team for so many years
He did a great job of bringing everyone together

timeline.text: F1 to introduce full-time race stewards from 2027

gist: Formula 1 will introduce permanent race stewards from the 2027 season.
The change addresses driver criticisms regarding inconsistent penalty decisions for on-track incidents.
Driver stewards and existing FIA stewards will continue to play a vital role.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The FIA announced it will introduce permanent race stewards starting in 2027 following consistent calls from grand prix drivers. A small number of full-time stewards will be recruited during 2027, with the group expanding from 2028.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Drivers have frequently complained that penalty rulings were applied inconsistently. The FIA stated that dedicated full-time stewards will provide continuity, expertise, and greater consistency in decision-making.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The FIA will begin recruiting permanent stewards for a phased introduction during the 2027 season, while continuing to use driver stewards and existing personnel on a mixed roster.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Max Verstappen and George Russell clashed during final practice for the Las Vegas Grand Prix. Verstappen was warned by stewards for an unpredictable change of direction under braking after overtaking Russell. Russell responded by pushing Verstappen wide, resulting in light contact between the cars.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The incident has reignited a long-standing rivalry between the two drivers, who have a history of public disputes. With both championships already decided, the personal animosity between the front-row starters provides a focal point for the remaining races of the season.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Verstappen and Russell are set to start the Las Vegas Grand Prix from the front row. The race is expected to be competitive, with the tow effect on the circuit potentially influencing the outcome and the battle for the constructors' championship.

timeline.text: Harden passes Bryant for 50-point games

gist: James Harden scored 51 points in a victory against the Indiana Pacers.
Harden surpassed Kobe Bryant for third place in all-time 50-point NBA games.
The 37-year-old recorded his 26th career 50-point performance during the NBA Cup.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: James Harden scored 51 points for the Cleveland Cavaliers in a 128-119 win against the Indiana Pacers. This performance marked his 26th career 50-point game, moving him past Kobe Bryant into third place on the all-time list. Harden, aged 37, also contributed six rebounds and six assists at Rocket Arena.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The achievement places Harden behind only Wilt Chamberlain and Michael Jordan in NBA history for 50-point games. Harden described the milestone as humbling and special, noting the difficulty of maintaining such impact in his 18th season.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The Cleveland Cavaliers are scheduled to play the Chicago Bulls on Tuesday.

timeline.text: Shevchenko accuses Mudryk camp of 'baseless slander'
Shevchenko lying about drugs test claims - Mudryk

gist: Andriy Shevchenko accused Mykhailo Mudryk's camp of seeking a false scapegoat for a doping test.
Mudryk blamed the Ukrainian Association of Football for his failed test and subsequent 20-month ban.
Shevchenko denied the allegations, defending the association and asking Mudryk to retract his comments.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Andriy Shevchenko stated that Mykhailo Mudryk's representatives repeatedly asked for a football federation employee to falsely take the blame for Mudryk's positive test for meldonium. Mudryk, suspended from November 2024 to July 2026, blamed the Ukrainian Association of Football for the failed test, claiming it happened on international duty and criticizing a lack of support.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Shevchenko called the claims baseless slander and defended the professionalism of association staff, while Mudryk argued the handling of the matter delayed his return to football.

fivew: Andriy Shevchenko accused Mykhailo Mudryk's representatives of asking an employee to falsely take the blame for a positive drugs test.
Mudryk blamed the Ukrainian Association of Football for his failed drugs test, prompting a public response from Shevchenko.

quotes.text: baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally
Head coach Serhiy Rebrov also approved for Mykhailo to have two of his personal specialists work with him at the training camps
